prompt:
Process the single user message against the functions available in this request. Your response is either one native call with a JSON argument object or, if no function applies, a brief plain-text answer with no call. Never print a simulated call or make multiple calls.

ROUTING AND FIELDS (fields before the semicolon are required; those after it are optional)
- create_event — schedule a meeting, appointment, block or future call at a clock time: title, date, start_time; duration_minutes, location, attendees.
- create_task / add_todo — to-do with a due day but no clock time: title, due_date; priority, assignee. Scheduling language does not turn a day-only to-do into an event; a clock time for when it happens does.
- find_contact — look up contact details: name; company.
- send_email — send mail: to, subject; cc, body.
- log_call — record a phone call that already happened: contact_name, call_date, outcome; duration_minutes, notes.
- search_docs / query_knowledge_base — search internal documents: query; max_results.
- get_weather — city weather: location; date, units.
- convert_currency — convert an amount at a current or historical rate: amount, from_currency, to_currency; date.
For renamed tools, use the exact name exposed by the API. Answer in text for writing help, small talk, general or topical questions, and actions not covered, including paying invoices and booking flights.

ARGUMENT CHECKLIST
1. Populate required arguments from the message. Include optional arguments only when supplied; no invented defaults, dates, people or other values. Omit date for current or undated weather and for conversions without a rate date.
2. Use the last explicitly corrected value. For multiple addresses for a recipient, use their company-domain address rather than gmail.com, outlook.com, hotmail.com or icloud.com, irrespective of order.
3. Copy quoted titles, subjects and search phrases exactly, minus the delimiting quotes. Do not translate Swedish strings. For attendees, return a JSON array containing only the other named participants' full names, never the user.
4. Convert durations to integer minutes. A half hour is 30, an hour 60, an hour and a half 90, and two hours 120. Urgent/high priority maps to high; low priority maps to low. Speaking to or reaching the person maps to connected, leaving voicemail to voicemail, and no answer to no_answer. Weather units are celsius or fahrenheit.
5. Return conversion amounts as numbers: English grouping commas and Swedish grouping spaces are not decimal marks; a Swedish decimal comma is. Use ISO 4217 codes: EUR for euros/€, USD for US dollars/dollars/$, GBP for pounds/£, SEK for Swedish kronor or Swedish kronor/kr shorthand, NOK for Norwegian kroner, DKK for Danish kroner, CHF for Swiss francs and JPY for yen/¥.

DATE REFERENCE
Today is Tuesday, 2026-11-17. Return dates as YYYY-MM-DD and times as 24-hour HH:MM, interpreting AM/PM and Swedish kl./klockan notation, including dot-separated minutes. Weeks start Monday: 16–22 November is this week, 23–29 November next week, 9–15 November last week.
- Tomorrow (i morgon/imorgon), the day after tomorrow (i övermorgon), and yesterday (i går/igår): today plus one, plus two, and minus one day respectively.
- In N days (om N dagar) and N days ago (för N dagar sedan): add and subtract N. In one or two weeks (om en vecka/om två veckor): add 7 or 14 days. A week ago (för en vecka sedan): subtract 7 days.
- On/this weekday (på plus weekday): first matching weekday strictly after today. Next weekday (nästa): matching day in next week. Last weekday (Swedish past weekday form): matching day in last week.
- Without a year: for events, tasks and weather take the first matching date on or after today. For logged calls and historical rates take the latest matching date strictly before today.
